daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Attorney General's Office intensified its investigation into corruption cases, with seven witnesses examined in the Free Nutritious Meals Program (MBG) corruption case, including partners of SPPG and foundation officials. In a separate case, the AGO continued proceedings against Febrie Adriansyah, with prosecutors citing inconsistent testimony as grounds for his detention and requesting rejection of his pre-trial challenge. The case also saw revelations that Cabinet Secretary Teddy contacted Lodewyk Pusung before he was removed from BGN and arrested by the AGO.

  • A senior DPR member rebuked the Minister of Religious Affairs over Saudi Arabia's blocking of Rp 66.6 billion in down payments for the 2027 hajj pilgrimage.
  • The Ministry of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection formed a working group to boost women's political representation, while the minister separately criticized the implementation of the 30 percent quota for female legislative candidates.
  • An DPR member commented on PPPK teachers becoming central government civil servants, calling for distribution according to regional needs, as Gus Fawait supported efforts to transition part-time PPPK to full-time status and eventually to permanent civil service.
  • Several DPR members and a former deputy police chief criticized the head of the Criminal Investigation Agency for failing to attend a legislative hearing.
  • PDI-P dispatched hospital ship Laksamana Malahayati to assist NTT earthquake victims and sent medicines and maternal supplies to the disaster zone.
  • A UI student leader debated with the Central Jakarta police chief during a demonstration in the HI roundabout area.
  • The Bogor city government enacted a local regulation on child protection to strengthen violence prevention measures.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent a diplomatic protest note to Saudi Arabia rejecting the blocking of Rp 66.6 billion in down payments for the 2027 hajj pilgrimage. The foreign ministry separately stated that Indonesia will focus on national capacity in responding to foreign offers of assistance for NTT earthquake victims. The Indonesian Navy seized 514 tons of illegal minerals during 2026 operations.

  • Indonesia expressed optimism that ties with Singapore will bolster ASEAN resilience, while Jakarta and Montevideo agreed to expand cooperation to boost commodity exports.
  • The Indonesia-China Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue focused on economic partnership issues, while the foreign minister departed to visit Australia and New Zealand to strengthen bilateral partnerships.
  • Indonesia denied US allegations of transshipment fraud in trade operations.
  • The TNI Commander promoted two soldiers who lowered the Moon and Star flag on Aceh Peace Day.
  • The search for missing Indonesian crew members in the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait continues.

Other

Vice President Gibran vowed government support for NTT earthquake survivors during his visit to the disaster zone, where he inspected damaged infrastructure from ports to churches and apologized to victims for any shortcomings in relief efforts. The disaster's toll continued to mount, with BNPB reporting the death toll reached 75, while 1,378 schools were affected, including 502 severely damaged, and 3,752 aftershocks had occurred.

  • Indonesia's free health check program has reached 82 million participants, with authorities stepping up screening to detect tuberculosis cases.
  • The National Energy Council identified nuclear energy as a potential "dark horse" for achieving Indonesia's net-zero emissions target.
  • The Transportation Ministry changed regulations governing the transportation of imported and exported goods, introducing five key new provisions.
  • A magnitude 4.6 earthquake struck Nagekeo regency in NTT.
  • Celebrity Ruben Onsu was named a suspect in an alleged investment fund embezzlement case.
